specification.rule: Without explicit fast-math environment or SignedZeroInfNanPreserve for the width, Vulkan assumes NSZ/NotInf/NotNaN independently of NoContraction. DenormPreserve retains subnormals; FAdd/FSub are correctly rounded under RTE. Exact bounded simplification introduces no reassociation or mode change. Applying this rule below is reviewer inference.

proof.bounded_nonzero: Magnitude <=0x7b800000 means finite |x|<=2^120. For nonzero x, native RTPack(x,+0,+0,+0) has five numerical TwoSum pairs (0,0),(x,0),(0,0),(x,0),(0,0). x+0 and x-x are exact, including subnormal x under DenormPreserve; no overflow, residual or radius is introduced. Direct [x,+0,+0,+0,1] is a permitted refinement.
proof.signed_input_zero: Direct [+0,+0,+0,+0,1] for either input-zero sign is likewise permitted by NSZ. The original RTE zero-tail chain admits these words (ordinary IEEE RTE -0 + +0 is +0). Zero fallback is not required by the inspected boundary. This does not prove every prior native lowering selected these words.
proof.invalid: The unchanged bit bound rejects all nonfinite and >2^120 inputs to exactly the original RTInvalid fields. No mere-finite widening or exceptional behavior change is justified.
proof.contract: RetainedValue exposes all three limbs and radius (20 bytes); IsRepresented checks finite bounds, validity, nonnegative radius and spacing. RTExact uses numeric zero equality. RPBits/RTNegate can observe zero signs, but do not upgrade the declared arithmetic environment to universal old-driver equality.
proof.precise_boundary: Existing memcmp ownership/capsule/repeat checks remain exact within actual executions. No requirement for bit equality across every admissible native lowering was found in these inspected declarations/tests.
